# Final SimplifyLocals retained-case review — agent judgment

Reviewed `.tmp/pass-review-followup-final-v133/simplify-locals`, native CLI SHA256 `4aa2af1acc077a246e33f0fcecf8dbc52de16a38f1dcb2a98f77af5405e88d0a`, verified Binaryen133 SHA256 `8f25e9fd5db0fc5f210003aaa432922feb2e52d309e430def2f929e34da9466b`. The summary, toolchain, all10,000 case records, every retained metadata/failure/WAT file, and all20 retained input/Binaryen/Starshine instruction patterns were inspected; every binary file was inventoried and hashed. Per-file size/hash inventory and per-case judgments are adjacent JSON files. `review_simplify.py` is a read-only static checker; it invokes no optimizer, compiler, or runtime.

The lane has380 matches and9,620 mismatches, zero command/validation failure statuses. Summary `normalized-match:380` duplicates the matching cases; it is not another380 comparisons. Every mismatch is canonically smaller. This size counter alone does not establish semantic correctness or a Starshine win. Runtime/semantic oracle is OFF in this campaign. Parent-managed baseline and Node replays are pending; no whole-pass universal runtime equivalence is claimed.

All20 retained cases are agent-judged proven scoped Starshine wins:12 differ only by deletion of Nop AST nodes;4 additionally commute an adjacent dropped global read with a dropped memory load;4 match one fully inspected family template after replacing only i32.const operands. All have strict raw AND canonical encoded size reductions. Canonical non-code sections match exactly. Raw import encodings can differ, but parsed import declarations match exactly and canonical imports match. No benchmark/time benefit is inferred from these byte counts.

## Primitive proof for retained differences

For12 Nop-only cases, parsed WAT ASTs are exactly equal after deleting standalone Nop nodes. Signatures, locals, label names, operands and instruction order remain equal. Nop has no value, side effect, trap or control transfer. This proves these retained changes preserve behavior, independently of validation.

For effect-order cases1,4,7,15, ASTs become equal after Nop deletion and moving an adjacent dropped nontrapping global.get across a dropped i32.load. The global read is discarded and cannot mutate state or trap. There is no call/global write or other operation between it and the load; memory loads retain their mutual order. A load trap has the same state and trap category on either ordering. This proof does not require assuming memory bounds, a particular mutable global value, or host memory contents. Canonical savings are6,10,15,15bytes (raw5,9,14,14bytes).

Family cases8,13,18,19 have identical input/Binaryen/Starshine templates after replacing only actual i32.const operands. Case13 was read function by function; the static checker verifies the exact constant-variant relation separately for all three programs, including resource declarations, labels, types, stores, calls and reference operations. The following arguments apply for all integer constant values, except the explicitly preserved fixed memory/table addresses discussed below:

- Functions0,1,2,3,5,9 differ only by Nop deletion between Binaryen and Starshine. This includes the branch payload, br_on_null block, result loop, and both ref.as_non_null operations. The potential null trap is retained exactly. Their other common transformations from input are outside this pairwise difference review.
- Function4 replaces a result If of two i32 constants with Select of those constants and the same unchanged parameter. Eager evaluation adds only nontrapping constants. The second If has a return arm: moving the local.set into its nonreturn arm preserves the return and makes the same write on the fallthrough path. The final result If selects a constant or the same untouched local; eager local.get cannot trap or mutate. Starshine drops that value instead of writing it into a local then discarding the now-dead local. There is no later use of that write and the function returns no value. Both condition values and branch/return behavior remain the same for every i32 parameter.
- Function6 removes a redundant dropped local.get and associated dead local traffic. Those local reads cannot trap or mutate; no value is returned. Parameter reads retained in both programs have the same index.
- Function7 reads/discards the global before the same global.set; replacing a saved old global value with an immediate drop cannot change the later set. Starshine captures the first memory load in a scratch local, then performs the second load and discards the captured value; this preserves the input load order. Binaryen swaps those two dropped reads. In these retained modules memory is defined nonshared with minimum1page, fixed addresses0and4 and width4, no imported aliases/calls/resize before the loads, and no memory mutation between them. Both are inbounds for all module states reachable here, so this pairwise read order difference cannot change a trap or effect. The third load stays BEFORE the same store in all programs; only the unobservable saved-value drop moves to the load site. Table.get/table.set index0, operands and order remain unchanged, and the same helper call remains after them. The inserted i32 scratch shifts the unused funcref local declaration but all remaining local uses refer to the correct scratch. This is a49byte canonical/53byte raw overall win despite one extra declared local; it is not evidence that every local-count metric improves.
- Function8 keeps the helper call before the same try_table. Starshine discards the call result immediately instead of saving and discarding it inside the protected body. The call remains outside that handler, executes exactly once, and has the same exception/trap frontier. Removing the nontrapping local.get/drop cannot throw into the handler. Catch tags/targets and the second protected constant-drop body remain the same. No effectful expression moves across an exception frame.

These are source/primitive-semantic arguments plus strict encoded-size advantage, not `valid+smaller` inference. Relevant production contracts are exact effect conflict checks in `simplify_locals.mbt` (`simplify_locals_sinkables_may_conflict`, effect masks and sparse local/global read/write facts), structured result rewriting and HOT lowering cleanup; concrete retained instruction trees are the authority for this scoped proof. GenValid family-coverage intentionally includes memory/table/global writes, branch payloads, return, TryTable and reference traps. It does not prove arbitrary new combinations or all possible exception/multivalue inputs.

## Coverage and remaining limits

Retained profiles are effect-order, structure-result, flat-parent, local-traffic and family-coverage. The full counters also include604 stress mismatches and181 dae2-locals mismatches with no retained bundle in this first20 cap. Those unretained cases are not individually classified as proven wins here. All9,620 mismatch records are smaller, but9600 unretained cases have only counter/profile evidence in this review; they cannot all inherit the20 specific proofs from size alone. This is a retained-artifact review, not a claim that the entire residual set is semantically proven.

Historical parity gaps from other seeds/profiles are not closed by this campaign. Parent owns their durable disposition, baseline replay and Node runtime followup. The exact strict matches and the20 scoped wins establish no new confirmed defect in the reviewed retained set. No source changes were made during this final campaign review.


## Final replay update (supersedes pending text above)

The final joint audit `/tmp/starshine-pass-goal-review/final-retained-runtime-audit.json` confirms every retained bundle is byte-identical to the starting baseline optimizer output. This establishes provenance, not correctness. All20 SimplifyLocals bundles match original-vs-Starshine observations:16 have exported function plans; the4family-coverage modules (8,13,18,19) have no function plan or start, so their replay covers only compilation/instantiation/resources. Their internal-function instruction proof above remains necessary. Binaryen runtime replay is blocked for effect-order cases1,4,7,15 by compact-import support; this is not a confirmed Binaryen semantic defect. Across all400 retained campaign cases,351 original/Starshine observations match (245with function plans,106compile/instantiate/resources only),49 originals are blocked (48timeouts,1stack-switching support);28additional Binaryen observations are blocked by compact imports/custom descriptors. No semantic mismatch was observed. These results do not extend runtime claims to all generated inputs or close unreviewed/historical parity gaps. Individual case JSON now records exact replay scope and source hash.

# Final whole-CLI evidence audit

Assessment: retained results are internally consistent. They prove a large full-CLI Flatten scaling gain on the four targeted fixtures, stable output bytes versus the clean baseline on48 cases, and no observed runtime difference in the80 saved Flatten observations. They do not prove that every changed pass is faster or uses less memory. Several command medians are higher, all their before/after command ranges overlap, and several pass-local timer series are absent.

## Identity and method

Read results.json, identity.json, flatten-runtime-results.json, both harnesses, C RSS runner source, and every retained plain/traced output hash. No compiler, benchmark rerun, production/test edit or campaign interference was performed. Only short version queries and wasm-tools printing of the383/384-byte compact-import fixture were executed.

Baseline native CLI: e3eb308c1b866a82900ba2e14a7e2340310e84f32386b94f5eebd39e3f560d07,15,576,984bytes. Final CLI:4aa2af1acc077a246e33f0fcecf8dbc52de16a38f1dcb2a98f77af5405e88d0a,15,753,808bytes. Both current files match retained identities. Native executable size increases176,824bytes (1.135%). This is native executable size, not emitted wasm size or resident memory.

Oracle hash8f25e9fd5db0fc5f210003aaa432922feb2e52d309e430def2f929e34da9466b was checked against the actual file; short query returns wasm-opt version133(version_133). Validator reports wasm-tools1.262.0(e22db44da2026-10-13); runtime reports Nodev26.11.1. Six input hashes and the measurement harness hash match retained identity.json. Platform is native x86_64 Linux; no cross/emulated runtime evidence is used.

Harness executes22 explicit passes on each of two modules plus Flatten on64/128/256/512 independent-control fixtures:48 cases. The artifact named small is192,893bytes; mixed is7,705bytes. Labels should not be treated as a monotone input-size scale. Per case/tool:2warmup+7measured fresh processes, alternating before/after/oracle then reverse. Tools use explicit matching pass flags; Binaryen uses --all-features and BINARYEN_CORES=1; GSI/GTO aliases are gsi/gto, and both Starshine and oracle use --closed-world only for those two passes.

Plain command timing includes process startup, C RSS wrapper, module I/O/decode, pass work, validation/encode/write and process teardown. RSS comes from a minimal C parent fork/exec/wait4, in LinuxKiB. Separate traced fresh processes measure canonical cumulative pass timers by taking their maximum total per process. These are not the same sample processes as plain command timing. Binaryen traces use BINARYEN_PASS_DEBUG=1. No per-object allocation or original clean compiler-time measurement is in this whole-CLI dataset.

## Integrity checks

-48 distinct expected cases, with exact expected pass/input coverage.
-1,296 plain plus1,296 traced processes: all status0, expected round/tool order and warmup flags.
-144 final traced output validations: all wasm-tools status0, with before/after/oracle coverage per case.
-All9 plain output hashes per tool/case are stable. All288 current retained plain/traced files match saved plain hashes. All traced outputs match plain outputs.
-All48 baseline/final output hashes independently match, with unchanged wasm byte sizes. This includes all four targeted Flatten outputs.
-All retained command/RSS medians, minima, maxima and sample counts reproduce exactly from the7 measured samples. There are no integrity discrepancies.

Twelve Starshine tool/case timer series (six cases times before/after) have no canonical pass timer: optimize-casts on both generic modules; ssa on both; precompute on small; ssa-nomerge on mixed. Report these as N/A, never zero or a measured pass-local speedup. Effective requested flags are retained in trace logs, but absent timers alone do not establish candidate work or execution cost.

## Performance and memory findings

Targeted Flatten full-CLI medians (ms), with exactly equal wasm bytes:

| Controls | Baseline command → final | Change | Baseline traced pass → final |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|64|4.852→3.830|-21.1%|1.421→0.275|
|128|8.642→4.087|-52.7%|5.276→0.507|
|256|24.805→5.219|-79.0%|20.750→0.919|
|512|78.856→7.663|-90.3%|76.718→1.750|

The four targeted command ranges do not overlap. The final256→512 pass timer grows1.90x, rather than the old3.70x, which supports removal of the observed quadratic path on this fixture family. Oracle512 command/pass medians are5.848/0.473ms; the final Starshine pass remains about3.70x slower on this fixture despite the improvement. No pass-local <=2x-oracle claim follows here.

Generic command medians increase on20cases and decrease on24; adding the four targeted Flatten gains gives28/48 decreases. Largest command increases: mixedGSI3.472→3.995ms(+15.1%), mixedoptimize-instructions9.145→10.281ms(+12.4%), mixedstring-gathering3.492→3.869ms(+10.8%), smallGTO4.676→5.061ms(+8.3%). Every command-regression case has overlapping before/after min/max ranges, so these are measured median regressions/signals, not isolated algorithmic regression proof.

The separate pass timers narrow the claim: mixedoptimize-instructions3.126→3.122ms is flat while its command median rises; mixedGSI152→166us(+9.2%); mixedcoalesce667→721us(+8.1%); mixedinlining450→487us(+8.2%). These remain visible limits. SmallDAE command21.277→19.335ms(-9.1%) has nonoverlapping command ranges and pass19.881→18.350ms(-7.7%). SmallDAE-optimizing command55.844→52.114ms(-6.7%) also has nonoverlapping command ranges, while its separate trace64.039→60.892ms(-4.9%) is inflated relative to plain total due to tracing. Traced and plain costs must not be mixed as one timing population.

Whole-command RSS median deltas range from-1,700KiB(Flatten512) to+452KiB(Flatten256). Generic maximum observed median increase is+444KiB(mixedstring-gathering); smallDAE+316KiB, DAE-optimizing/inlining+292KiB. Most deltas are small process/allocator effects; this dataset neither measures direct allocations nor proves a universal memory decrease. Read the full ranges in case-table.md/audit.json before using a median as an exact footprint.

Many final Starshine pass-local medians still exceed Binaryen (e.g.smallDAE18.350ms vs0.646ms, smallDAE-optimizing60.892ms vs5.560ms, mixedinlining-optimizing1.057ms vs0.094ms). All these small-fixture measured pass times are below1second, but that does not establish artifact-scale performance or broad parity. Emitted output byte sizes differ from Binaryen across many cases; smaller valid output alone is not a semantic-equivalence proof or a Starshine-win classification. This audit did not classify those existing output-shape families.

## Flatten runtime observations and normalization

Five fixtures times four arguments(-1,0,1,2) times original/baseline/final/oracle yield80 observations. All saved observation arrays exactly match originals, including integer results, imported calls and order. The distinct fixture explicitly expects single7,pair10,pair11,single8,pair21-or22,single9. Both If arms are exercised; four scaling fixtures check exact producer counts64/128/256/512. All final values are constant0 and most derived tuple arithmetic is dropped: this is strong producer-count/order coverage, not broad arithmetic-result, GC, trap, EH, memory, or randomized semantic coverage.

One Binaryen distinct-order output uses compact imports, which Node26 cannot execute directly. Harness reruns the same oracle pass with only --disable-compact-imports, validates the expanded file, and requires every non-import/non-custom section byte-equal. This reviewer independently rechecked that equality and compared the printed declarations: both encode env.pair as function0/type1 and env.single as function1/type0 in the same order; type-section bytes are identical. Raw383bytes and expanded384bytes are an encoding-only compatibility control. The80-observation oracle claim for that fixture refers to the expanded encoding, not direct execution of the raw compact-import bytes. normalization-audit.json retains both hashes and decoded import identities.

## Limits and open evidence

Seven measured samples per side do not provide a statistical confidence interval or guarantee stable microsecond differences. Workload coverage is two fixed generic modules plus one repeated-control family and a distinct-order fixture. No original cold compiler time was recorded, so the1.135% executable growth cannot be converted into a compiler-time claim. The plain harness clears STARSHINE_TRACING but does not explicitly clear inherited BINARYEN_PASS_DEBUG; historical inherited environment is not retained, so trace absence for every plain oracle process cannot be proven from raw stderr (which plain samples do not save on success). Traced equality and stable hashes are good controls but do not substitute for absent historical environment records.

This evidence supports the specific measured gains above with unchanged baseline outputs. It does not support blanket approval that all performance/footprint issues are eliminated. Dedicated pass-local allocation controls, existing correctness regressions, fullCI, reviewed semantic replay and final GenValid campaigns remain separate signoff evidence.

# Final control pass artifact review

Read-only review of all100 retained bundles:20 each for remove-unused-brs,ssa,ssa-nomerge,flatten and merge-blocks, from `.tmp/pass-review-followup-final-v133/`. Campaign Starshine CLI SHA256 `4aa2af1acc077a246e33f0fcecf8dbc52de16a38f1dcb2a98f77af5405e88d0a`; verified Binaryen133 SHA256 `8f25e9fd5db0fc5f210003aaa432922feb2e52d309e430def2f929e34da9466b`. Source identities are in `reviewed-source-identities.json`. No production edit, build, native benchmark, heavy tool or runtime replay was performed during this review.

No confirmed semantic defect was found in these retained cases. This is not a strict structural-parity pass:50,000 cases were compared;22,420 structural mismatches remain in the five lane reports. All five report0validation,property,generator and command failures. The separate parent raw baseline/Node replay remains required; a zero failure counter does not establish which optional properties were exercised.

## Agent judgments

| Pass | Compared | Structural mismatch | Retained scoped wins | Retained open size/parity gaps |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
|remove-unused-brs|10000|2727|6|14|
|ssa|10000|1287|12|8|
|ssa-nomerge|10000|6250|20|0|
|flatten|10000|9163|20|0|
|merge-blocks|10000|2993|20|0|

Every retained case has a separate judgment, raw/canonical sizes, source reasoning, proof results and nine artifact hashes in `case-judgments.json`. `CASES.md` is the compact100-row index. `open-cases.json` preserves all22 open retained examples. These classifications are agent judgments; they are not harness-provided facts.

## Evidence and source reasoning

All100 input instruction streams were decoded read-only (`input-instruction-audit.json`). All canonical module trees were parsed and compared (`structural-proof.json`); per-case full diffs are retained. The small abstract evaluator supports only explicit pure folded constants/locals/tuple/select/control and rejects unsupported operations. It compares exact function outcomes under symbolic typed parameters, traps or repeated pure loop state. It is an audit aid, not a general Wasm validator or a replacement for raw native/Node execution.

Remove-unused-brs: the two tuple-drop cases preserve11/13 lanes while eliminating unobserved local copies, saving12B canonically and14B raw. The four EH cases use one local no-payload tag caught by its exact surrounding try_table arm; caught throw, branch to the enclosing void block and final fallthrough have the same observable exit, with3B canonical savings and equal raw sizes. The source guards in `remove_unused_brs_match_caught_throw` reject uncertain imported-tag aliases and reference-catching arms. The large cleanup/GC/control/switch cases contain no calls or external state/heap operations: GC types are declarations, runtime references are null constants, and all functions' symbolic return vectors agree. Their canonical savings do not close their raw-size losses. Sink-block cases skip only nops; replacing their void branch with an empty eqz If retains condition evaluation, but raw+4B remains open.

SSA:13 retained typed-control cases have the same one-input loop and condition0 backedge. The raw writer retains the original typed-loop header while fresh/merge definitions preserve incoming parameter and canonical0/1 local versions. This avoids redundant HOT/Binaryen legalization carrier tees/copies: all13 canonical outputs are4B smaller and symbolic all-parameter behavior agrees. Twelve are scoped wins; case94 is still raw+1B and therefore open. Seven unreachable cases start with an unconditional trap, and their canonical bodies are exactly unreachable; one dead local declaration differs. Canonical size is equal and raw Starshine bytes are9–21B larger, so they remain size-losing parity gaps.

SSA-nomerge: eight smoke cases are exact complete-module identities after deleting one NOP, saving1B raw and canonically. Twelve stress/coverage cases are canonical identities after removing three unreferenced i32 declarations, but the raw18B saving is not declaration encoding. Raw bytecode audit (`raw-exact-proof.json`, `raw-nomerge-instructions.json`) shows removal of an outer block and dead local-read/null-throwref try_table tail, plus an unreachable marker after a terminal branch. Before any changed tail, both raw instruction streams have the identical first loop: local1:=1; br_if self(local1). It never exits for any parameter. No live branch targets the removed outer frame; the only prefix table targets its own inner block. Other function instructions are byte-identical. Some raw type orders differ, but resolved defined-function signatures and every non-type/function/code section agree. Thus these are scoped raw-size wins only: canonical size is equal, and no runtime gain is claimed.

Flatten: all20 retained cases cover nine fixed generator families and have smaller raw and canonical encodings (2–394B canonical savings). Payloads are captured once before br/br_if/br_table and the same carriers cover taken and false-flow exits; typed tuple lanes and reverse drop order are retained. Tee storage remains before dependent multiply, with no intervening write before the direct read. Untargeted loops have no backedges and execute once; their entry16 is preserved before adding1. The legacy Try body only computes35+36, cannot throw, and returns71; catch37 uses the same mutually exclusive carrier. The unreachable family traps before all later work. Source/IR inspection plus exact pure symbolic function outcomes support the scoped wins; size and validation alone were not used. The performance certificate/prefix changes preserve this transform contract. No retained case separately proves all remaining If/function-result family outputs.

MergeBlocks: all20 retained bundles have the same fixed expression-profile input hash. After deleting exactly two If-arm NOPs, their complete canonical trees are identical, including memory Store and tag Throw order. The raw decoded instruction streams are also exact after only those NOP deletions; non-code sections and function signatures are unchanged. Both raw and canonical sizes save2B. The fixed generator constructor and profile count2993 agree with aggregate5986B savings, but this does not mean each suppressed output was independently inspected. NOP removal comes from HOT lowering cleanup and does not erase the If condition or effectful expression children.

## Open losses and limits

The full-lane raw-size counters report8110 larger Starshine outputs for remove-unused-brs and9155 for SSA, even though neither lane has a larger canonical output. Aggregate raw deltas are+159331B and+83194B respectively. Those raw output costs remain visible; canonical benefits are not treated as blanket closure. Retained open examples comprise14remove-unused-brs cases (raw+4..148B) and8SSA cases (raw+1..21B). `open-cases.json` records each exact delta and semantic relation.

The retained cap is20 per lane. Suppressed structural residuals are not silently classified as semantically proved. Flatten's retained cases cover nine of twelve fixed profiles; If and function-results are unretained here, and operand cases structurally match. Fewer local declarations alone was not counted as a canonical or runtime win. The12nomerge raw-only wins explicitly use raw source/control proof plus18B size savings, with canonical equality.

These generated retained cases do not directly exercise the original nondefaultable cross-frame SSA repair or the removed-If-label bug: targeted default TDD regressions remain the evidence for those fixes. Likewise, the final MergeBlocks retained family is only NOP cleanup; the separate scalar-header12fixture v133 size/execution proof remains at `/tmp/starshine-scalar-header-review/` with independent assessment `/tmp/starshine-control-review/scalar-header-review.md`.
